zh: 我们对此非常有条理。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can regularly keep pulse of everything.
zh: 我可以定期掌握一切的脉搏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Getting that felt sense of intuition and sentiment is what's important to me.
zh: 获得那种直觉和情绪的感知觉对我很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm very data-driven, but an intuitive decision maker, layering the data into it.
zh: 我非常数据驱动，但也是一个直觉决策者，将数据分层放入其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're not getting that, if you don't have a process by which to glean that, then...
zh: 所以如果你没有得到那个，如果你没有一个过程来收集那个，那么……

speaker: Unknown
en: You're often operating blind.
zh: 你经常在盲目运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe that the best way to make a decision is getting as close to the customer as possible.
zh: 我相信做出决定的最佳方式是尽可能贴近客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And often the people on the front lines have the answer.
zh: 而且通常前线的人员都有答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just like sitting over here like pontificating.
zh: 我们就像坐在这儿夸夸其谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to me, it's often like, let's bring the people who actually are close to this into the discussion either directly or like, let's make sure we're getting their input.
zh: 所以对我来说，这通常就像，让我们让实际上接近这些情况的人参与到讨论中，要么直接参与，要么比如，让我们确保我们得到了他们的意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen this in both ways.
zh: 我从两个方面都见过这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been like, you know, in an organization where people are making decisions with completely lacking context.
zh: 我曾待过，你知道，在一个人们做决定完全缺乏背景的组织里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would think one of the things you spent some time working on in your role is incentive design.
zh: 我想你在你的职位上花时间处理的事情之一是激励设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, maybe in the most extreme, there's so many important things as it relates to running a go-to-market team and figuring out things like com.
zh: 我的意思是，也许在最极端的情况下，有很多重要的事情与运营市场投放团队和弄清楚诸如提成之类的事情有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of the things that you figured out as it relates to incentive design or mistakes that you've had to correct or things like that as you try to figure out how to incent and align many, many, many, many people?
zh: 关于激励设计，你弄清楚了一些什么，或者你不得不纠正了一些什么错误，或者当你试图弄清楚如何激励和协调许许多多的人时，类似这样的事情是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the biggest experience I've had in this and learnings has been in the, like, sales compensation and moving from a SaaS model to consumptive.
zh: 我的意思是，我在这个方面最大的经验和学习是在，比如，销售薪酬方面，以及从 SaaS 模式转向消费模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at Google, we were in G Suite, a SaaS, like, you book a deal, like, you give rep credit, you don't really have to do anything.
zh: 所以在 Google，我们在 G Suite，一个 SaaS，比如，你签了一个单，你给代表记功，你真的不需要做任何其他事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's incredible.
zh: 这真是不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then whereas consumptive, you have to close the deal, they have to ramp, you have to predict how much they're going to spend.
zh: 而对于消费模式，你必须完成交易，他们必须逐步增加，你必须预测他们会花多少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I've lived through this transition twice now.
zh: 所以我已经经历了两次这样的转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I came into Checkr, people were comped on bookings.
zh: 当我进入 Checkr 时，人们的薪酬是基于预订的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like how much the customer is going to spend.
zh: 这就像是客户会花多少钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much do you think they're going to spend?
zh: 你认为他们会花多少钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: In reality, we don't collect revenue until based on how many checks they're running.
zh: 实际上，我们要根据他们运行多少次检查才能收取收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so people were getting way overpaid for things that maybe weren't going live or the actual revenue realization was very different than expected.
zh: 所以人们拿到的报酬远超实际，针对那些可能没有上线的事情，或者实际的收入实现与预期非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So incentives were completely off.
zh: 所以激励完全错了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we had to do a pretty dramatic change.
zh: 所以我们必须做一个相当戏剧性的改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're doing this with companies we acquire, too, where you're comped on revenue.
zh: 我们对我们收购的公司也是这样做的，在那里你的薪酬是基于收入的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, therefore, I know if you're comped on this, your pay is aligning with value to the customer, which is then aligning with revenue to Checkr.
zh: 然后，因此，我知道如果你的薪酬是基于这个，你的报酬就与对客户的价值保持一致，然后也就与 Checkr 的收入保持一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've had to, like, tweak some things here and there.
zh: 我们必须，比如，在这里和那里调整一些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what's some sort of leading thing we can give them when the deal is closed?
zh: 比如，当交易完成时，我们可以给他们什么样的前期东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's been a game changer in terms of the way, like, customer engagement because we're doing what's right for them.
zh: 但这在...方面是一个游戏规则改变者，比如，客户参与度，因为我们正在做对他们来说是正确的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not just overselling them on something or overbooking things.
zh: 我们不仅仅是向他们过度推销或过度预订。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then making sure that they're going live and that rep is like very attuned to make sure that that all happens seamlessly.
zh: 然后确保他们上线，那个代表就像非常协调，以确保所有这些都无缝发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a big one.
zh: 这是一个大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it all comes down to what are we trying to achieve as a company?
zh: 我认为这都归结为我们作为一家公司试图实现什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is this person uniquely positioned to influence?
zh: 这个人处于独特的位置去影响什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you give them someone too much...
zh: 如果你给他们某人太多...

speaker: Unknown
en: Scope, then they're not getting incented on anything.
zh: 范围，那么他们就没有得到任何激励。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if I'm comping my sales leader on total revenue for the company, that's not high leverage for me.
zh: 比如如果我对我的销售领导根据公司的总收入支付报酬，那对我来说不是高杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then just giving them the guardrails so that we don't go out of bounds.
zh: 然后只是给他们护栏，这样我们就不会越界。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a sales incentive comp, if you do all those things and then you can set up to have a winning sales organization, then it's like these decisions are easy.
zh: 对于销售激励薪酬，如果你做了所有这些事情，然后你可以建立一个获胜的销售组织，那么就像这些决定很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Should we add more reps?
zh: 我们应该增加更多代表吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we treat this one?
zh: 我们怎么处理这一个？

speaker: Unknown
en: It just makes everything easier than if you have like the shadow approach that's not aligned with your company's success.
zh: 这只是让一切变得更容易，如果你有那种与公司成功不一致的影子方法的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And oftentimes, like for founders or for leaders, like a sales leader will come in and say like, no, no, no, we need to do it this way.
zh: 而且很多时候，比如对于创始人或领导者，比如一个销售领导者会进来说，不，不，不，我们需要用这种方式做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, no, you don't.
zh: 比如，不，你不需要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really think first principles.
zh: 真的要思考第一性原理。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the reflections you have about variable comp for sales?
zh: 你对销售的可变薪酬有什么思考？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I feel like you have a bunch of, you know, founders that want to think everything from first principles and a lot of them begin with,
zh: 因为我觉得你有一群，你知道，创始人想要从第一性原理思考一切，其中许多人开始于，

speaker: Unknown
en: There shouldn't be variable comp for reps. And in the fullness of time, I think that basically every single one of them eventually gets to the point that says, no, we should have variable comp.
zh: 代表不应该有可变薪酬。随着时间的推移，我认为基本上每一个创始人最终都会达到那个点，说不，我们应该有可变薪酬。

speaker: Unknown
en: There should be sales commissions.
zh: 应该有销售提成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've always wondered why aren't more PMs on variable comp and why aren't we pick any of these functions?
zh: 我一直想知道为什么更多的 PM 没有采用可变薪酬，为什么我们不挑选这些职能中的任何一个？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I haven't thought deeply about the product or other functions like engineers.
zh: 是的，我的意思是，我没有深入思考产品或其他职能如工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: But on the sales side, absolutely, they should be on variable comp.
zh: 但在销售方面，绝对，他们应该采用可变薪酬。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by nature, you want people who are incredibly competitive, hungry, and who are going to take this risk of 50% of their compensation is at risk.
zh: 而且从本质上讲，你需要那些极其好胜、渴望，并且愿意承担他们的 50% 薪酬处于风险之中这种风险的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, sometimes I get asked, like, why do salespeople make so much?
zh: 比如，有时我被问到，为什么销售人员赚那么多？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like...
zh: 我就像……

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to go take a quota and have your salary cut in half?
zh: 你想拿配额然后把薪水减半吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how about it, right?
zh: 比如，怎么样，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like that would be interesting.
zh: 我觉得那会很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like a PM should be able to say, I'd like to be eligible for 40% more comp, but I'll cut my base by half.
zh: 我觉得 PM 应该能说，我想有资格多拿 40% 的薪酬，但我愿意把底薪减半。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the hard thing there, which is, I think, love any thoughts you have, but measuring the effectiveness of the... Inputs and outputs.
zh: 我认为那里的难点在于，我觉得，我很想听听你的想法，但要衡量投入和产出的有效性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, is hard.
zh: 是的，很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we talk about this all the time.
zh: 我们一直在讨论这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you know you have a high-functioning org?
zh: 你怎么知道你有一个高效的组织？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it the number of things they ship?
zh: 是他们发布东西的数量吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it the quality?
zh: 是质量吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's harder.
zh: 这更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the harder it is to have that scoreboard that you can look at objectively, the harder it is to put on a variable com.
zh: 我认为，拥有那个你能客观查看的记分牌越难，实施浮动薪酬就越难。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you are very clear on the input that's made, the output that they're driving...
zh: 但当你对所做投入、他们驱动的产出非常清晰时……

speaker: Unknown
en: And that there's, it's like a non-negotiable, very clear scorecard.
zh: 而且那是不可商量的，非常清晰的记分卡。

speaker: Unknown
en: It works well.
zh: 效果很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like MBO plans where you're, I've done those for certain roles where it's like, it's like five categories and you're rated on them at the end.
zh: 有那种 MBO 计划，我在某些角色做过这种，就是大概五个类别，最后按这些给你评级。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just like a ton of overhead.
zh: 那简直就是大量的开销。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't drive as much the same behavior.
zh: 它不能驱动那么多相同的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like sales success breeds people staying.
zh: 而且销售成功会让人们留下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Enterprise AE is like a hot commodity.
zh: 企业级 AE 是个抢手货。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can go other places.
zh: 他们可以去别的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they know there's going to make a lot more money or be more successful somewhere else, they'll vote with their feet.
zh: 如果他们知道在其他地方能赚更多钱或更成功，他们会用脚投票。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you want to have a good plan where there's a lot of upside.
zh: 所以你想要有一个好的计划，里面有很多上升空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the other thing we've looked at is like, I think you can get really stingy and be like, oh, this...
zh: 这是我们看过的另一件事，我想，你可能会变得非常小气，然后说，噢，这个……

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you know, we have accelerators.
zh: 比如，你知道，我们有加速器。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're making above your quota, it's going to go to accelerator mode.
zh: 如果你超额完成配额，就会进入加速器模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've had times where, like, there's caps on that or we're stingy on that.
zh: 我们有过这样的时期，比如，那上面有上限或者我们在那上面很小气。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, that's not the right move.
zh: 就像是，那不是正确的举动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, to what end?
zh: 比如，为了什么目的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if your unit economics are working, if you've done the math right, which you should be doing, then it all makes sense.
zh: 如果你的单位经济模型行得通，如果你把数学算对了——你应该这么做——那么这就都说得通了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, this math works.
zh: 就像，这个数学算得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people, like, the highest performing AE should make a lot more than a lot of people in the company.
zh: 我认为，就像，表现最好的 AE 应该比公司里的很多人赚得多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does feel like the fact that the work tends to be easier to measure makes it easier to comp in that way.
zh: 感觉确实是因为工作往往更容易衡量，才使得那样设置薪酬更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is that there's an unfortunate part of that, right?
zh: 这其中有不幸的部分，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because like a superstar, theoretically, maybe the average PM should be comped at x, but maybe the superstar PM should make 3x or whatever.
zh: 因为就像一个超级明星，理论上，也许普通的 PM 应该拿到 x 的薪酬，但也许超级明星 PM 应该拿 3 倍或者随便多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, you have career ladders and this and that, but it doesn't work the same way as sellers.
zh: 是的，你有职业阶梯等等，但这不像销售那样运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's where things are moving more and more, is differentiating, paying more for performance across all roles.
zh: 我认为这就是事情发展的方向，越来越多的差异化，所有角色都为绩效支付更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And especially with leveraging AI, you can get 10x more out of a certain amazing engineer than an average one.
zh: 特别是利用 AI，你可以从一个优秀的工程师身上比普通工程师多获得 10 倍的产出。

speaker: Unknown
en: In working across so many sellers, what's kind of your working theory if you take in any team that you've worked on and you look at the number one seller versus everyone else?
zh: 在与这么多销售人员合作中，如果你看看你合作过的任何团队，看看头号销售和其他人相比，你的工作理论是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they always doing something consistently different than, not what is difference between the best one and the worst, but the folks that are good and the person that's like the head and shoulder star on the team?
zh: 他们是否总是在做些不同的事情，不是最好的和最差的区别，而是那些做得不错的人和团队中那个鹤立鸡群的明星之间的区别？

speaker: Unknown
en: People, like, have the misconception about sellers.
zh: 人们，就像，对销售人员有误解。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like, oh, it's the most, like, outgoing guy over there that's going to be the best seller.
zh: 他们会说，噢，那边那个最外向的家伙会是最好的销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of them are very introverted, I find.
zh: 我发现他们很多人非常内向。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to turn it on, you know, and then need to re-energize.
zh: 他们必须打开开关，你知道，然后需要重新充电。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's probably two ingredients for me.
zh: 对我来说可能有两个要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, like, building trust with customers, being able to do that is a gift, and it's something, or it's something that's a skill that you have to really develop.
zh: 我的意思是，比如，与客户建立信任，能够做到这一点是一种天赋，或者说这是一种你必须真正培养的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: But outside of that, I think it's really diligent, strategic thinking and planning.
zh: 但除此之外，我认为这真的是勤奋的、战略性的思考和规划。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like thinking through, what are all the moves I'm going to make?
zh: 这就像是在思考，我要做的所有举措是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I structure those?
zh: 我该如何构建那些？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I rally all the resources?
zh: 我如何集结所有资源？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a team sport.
zh: 这是一项团队运动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do that in a thoughtful, like a captain of a team.
zh: 而我以一种深思熟虑的方式做到这一点，就像一个团队的队长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think reps who don't, who are good...
zh: 我认为那些不……那些优秀的代表……

speaker: Unknown
en: Even that are IC reps, they have to think about the world that way.
zh: 即使他们是 IC 代表（个人贡献者代表），他们也得那样思考这个世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to think about the world that way.
zh: 他们必须那样思考这个世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're just exceptional at like the drive, the tenacity of executing that strategy.
zh: 他们在驱动力、执行该战略的毅力方面表现得非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're not flying by the seat of their pants.
zh: 他们不是在凭感觉行事。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not doing it on their own and then be like, oh, I got to bring along an SE or, oh, like this is, I didn't get approval for this last minute.
zh: 他们不是自己单干然后才说，哦，我得带上一个 SE，或者，哦，这个，我最后一刻才获批。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I see a lot of that, but the great ones are like exceptional project managers in a way at like thinking through how to get into the customer and like bring all the resources around them.
zh: 我是说，我看到很多这样的情况，但优秀的那些人在某种程度上是出色的项目经理，能够思考如何打入客户内部并调动周围的所有资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: Going back to sort of the transition from CRO to COO, did you find it at all hard not to just spend time and focus on all the stuff you're already very good at?
zh: 回到从 CRO 到 COO 的转型，你是否觉得完全不把时间和精力花在你已经非常擅长的事情上很难？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I would imagine you spent a career in various flavors of go-to-market.
zh: 比如，我想象你整个职业生涯都在各种不同形式的 go-to-market 中度过。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're very good at it because you're still doing it.
zh: 你非常擅长这个，因为你还在做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're the COO, but you know, the CRO hat kind of keeps calling you back because you're, you know, really good at that thing.
zh: 所以你是 COO，但你知道，那顶 CRO 的帽子总在召唤你回去，因为你，你知道，真的很擅长那件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, no, absolutely.
zh: 是的，不，绝对是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the ongoing push, you know, that I'm looking at.
zh: 这也是我正在关注的持续的压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, where am I spending my time working on with Daniel?
zh: 比如，我把时间花在和 Daniel 一起做什么上？

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, what are the next big strategic things we need to be thinking about?
zh: 还有，我们需要思考的下一个重大战略事项是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: One of those, for example, is a company we acquired recently or a year ago at this point, but integrating that in across the whole company and accelerating that business.
zh: 其中一件事，例如，是我们最近或一年前收购的一家公司，但要在全公司范围内整合它并加速该业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's like a go-to-market angle, but like really leaning in more directly.
zh: 所以这就像是一个 go-to-market 的角度，但更直接地深入参与。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard because I don't have a CRO.
zh: 这很难，因为我没有 CRO。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm still managing all of the functions as an effective CRO, but I have exceptional leaders.
